searchText: Just thinking out loud a bit, this forward/backward jump is only specified for RJUMPs in the spec (?) so only within the code section itself. Can't we also do the same for CALLF / JUMPF ? The forward jump requirement for the code sections (RJUMPs), I think this was added as requirement to the spec at some point? This makes the verification of unreachable code sections easier - right? (I remember before we had this requirement we had a somewhat complex branching-like algorithm to check this?) i think if you allow backwards only jumps then you need to re-traverse the same code during validation, maybe it can blow up the algorithm (maybe! i'm not sure, haven't thought about this in awhile) Ah no, in an older version of the EIP the algorithm was described (it was more complex with some branching) but still only checked each opcode once https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/blob/ce9748cc0881632974943ad55f67518dde8a8de1/EIPS/eip-5450.md hm yea i'm not sure why backwards jump is not allowed for code reachability check. maybe <@425274498732916736> knows? btw, spec nit: i noticed that `INVALID` is not actually explicitly defined in eof spec maybe it should have explicit carveout, otherwise it's not clear that INVALID is an "assigned" instruction https://github.com/ipsilon/eof/blob/ac91da4f6b4cbe03a423a7d6737ba99f9bc21950/spec/eof.md#code-validation in legacy evm, `INVALID` behavior is implicit (same behavior as any unassigned instruction, i.e. exceptional halt). but there are no unassigned instructions in EOF, so it needs definition I'm rather sure it is in the spec https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3670 its here aha -- i was looking at the mega spec Yes it is not explicit in the mega spec that's true Forward reference is only a rule in-section. The code sections have no such restriction, so you will need a work list to detect dead code there i.e. you can CALLF section 3 and it can then CALLF section 2 and that can be the only call to section 2. is there any opcode ranges that are safe to assume won't be assigned in the L1 EVM and could be defined in a rollup's EVM? I see C0..F0 is completely unassigned but for something like a snark-friendly hash function we'd want to expose like SHA3 is, would it be more reasonable to define that in the 21..30 range? EOF has opcodes in the 0xDx range and 0xEx range, so only 0xB0-0xCF is fully open. I think this is a good subject for the RollCall. Also, I think EOF would be well suited to this because we can signal capabilities in the header. I was going to write this on the way back from kenya but chose sleep instead 😉 My main concern with opcode experimentation is inadvertent collisions, so singaling what you are doing would be essential. What I have envisioned is another section like subcontainers, except instead of containing EOF they contain signals about what EIPs are enabled. Each capability would be readable text similar to "EIP-7692/1.0.0/..." where the first item is the EIP, the second is the EIP-7577 version number (https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/8034/files), and anything after that is EIP dependent. Dropped if it doesn't matter. With such a header, mainnet will always reject experimental containers, and rollups can write code to make informed decisions about wether or not to accept such containers.
